title: Advanced Graph Algorithms and Applications
description: This module explores advanced graph algorithms essential for solving complex real-world problems efficiently. You'll learn shortest path algorithms including Dijkstra's and Bellman-Ford, minimum spanning tree algorithms like Prim's and Kruskal's, and topological sorting for DAGs. The module also covers graph applications such as network routing, cycle detection in directed graphs, and strongly connected components. These powerful tools will equip you to tackle graph-based challenges in domains like social networks, transportation, and dependency management.

lessons.title: Dijkstra's Algorithm: Shortest Path in Weighted Graphs
lessons.content: Dijkstra's algorithm finds the shortest path from a single source to all other vertices in a graph with non-negative edge weights. It uses a priority queue (min-heap) to greedily select the nearest vertex not yet processed. Common applications include GPS navigation and network routing.

lessons.title: Implementing Dijkstra's Algorithm in JavaScript
Bellman-Ford Algorithm: Handling Negative Weights
lessons.content: Bellman-Ford algorithm finds shortest paths in graphs that may have negative edge weights and detects negative cycles. It relaxes all edges repeatedly and updates distances. If distances update after |V|-1 iterations, a negative cycle exists.

lessons.title: Implementing Bellman-Ford in JavaScript
Prim's Algorithm for Minimum Spanning Tree (MST)
lessons.content: Prim's algorithm builds a minimum spanning tree by starting from any vertex and greedily adding the cheapest edge that connects the tree to a new vertex. Useful in designing network layouts minimizing cable length or cost.

lessons.title: Kruskal's Algorithm for MST
lessons.content: Kruskal’s algorithm sorts all edges by weight and adds them one by one to the MST, skipping those that form cycles. It uses a Disjoint Set Union (DSU) or Union-Find data structure for cycle detection.

lessons.title: Implementing Kruskal's Algorithm with Union-Find
Topological Sorting of Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs)
lessons.content: Topological sort orders vertices in a DAG so that for every directed edge u -> v, u comes before v. Used in task scheduling, build systems, and resolving dependencies.

lessons.title: Topological Sort Implementation (DFS Approach)
Detecting Cycles in Directed Graphs
lessons.content: Cycle detection in directed graphs uses DFS with recursion stack tracking. If a node is visited again while still in recursion stack, a cycle exists. Important for detecting circular dependencies.

lessons.title: Strongly Connected Components (SCC) and Kosaraju's Algorithm
lessons.content: Strongly Connected Components are subgraphs where every vertex is reachable from every other vertex. Kosaraju’s algorithm finds SCCs in two DFS passes: one on the graph and one on the reversed graph.

lessons.title: Applications of Advanced Graph Algorithms
lessons.content:
- **Network Routing:** Shortest path for data packets.
- **Project Scheduling:** Using topological sort to manage tasks.
- **Detecting Deadlocks:** Cycle detection in resource allocation.
- **Map and GIS Systems:** MST for efficient infrastructure.
- **Social Network Analysis:** Identifying communities (SCC).

These algorithms form the backbone of many software and real-world systems.
